prompt.context: Our client is an online dating startup named Grad-U-Date, which specializes in matching graduate students with other graduate students. Grad-U-Date has finished building their app and are now looking for your assistance in deciding on a monetization strategy.
prompt.question: What is Grad-U-Date's best method of monetization? How profitable will the company be?

clarifying_info.q: What is the gender split of users?
clarifying_info.a: Gender ratio of users will be 50/50.

clarifying_info.q: Which student types are considered professional?
clarifying_info.a: MBA, law and medical students are considered professional students.

clarifying_info.q: What is the cost basis for the app build?
clarifying_info.a: The app has already been built and is considered a sunk cost.
Grad-U-Date will only operate within the United States.
There are 4 major competitors and hundreds of small competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other dating services focused on graduate students?
clarifying_info.a: There are currently no other online dating services that focus only on graduate students.

clarifying_info.q: Can multiple revenue models be used simultaneously?
clarifying_info.a: Only one revenue model can be used.

exhibits.title: Student Enrolment Information
exhibits.shows: A bar chart of new graduate students per university per year by program type, with a note that there are 1,000 universities in the United States. Each bar also shows the number of years required to complete the degree.

exhibits.title: Product Usage and Revenue Model Parameters
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the forecasted percentage of graduate students using Grad-U-Date under each revenue model, plus a description of the pricing parameters for each model.

data.Premium Account: $5 per month; 40% of men and 20% of women purchase premium accounts

exhibits.title: Online Dating Market Trends
exhibits.shows: A dual-axis chart tracking (left axis) the percentage of online dating users paying a monthly fee and (right axis) the average monthly fee in dollars, from 2008 to 2014.

data.Trend: Both the share of users paying a monthly fee and the average monthly fee have been declining since approximately 2008–2012, with a sharp drop starting in 2013

framework: Market size: estimate the total addressable graduate student population in the US
Competitive landscape: assess number and type of competitors and Grad-U-Date's differentiation
Monetization models: brainstorm options, identify pros and cons of each
Profitability analysis: calculate revenue and profit for each viable model using Exhibit 2 data
Recommendation: select the highest-profit model that is sustainable given market trends

questions.prompt: What types of monetization models could Grad-U-Date use, and what are the advantages and disadvantages of each?
questions.guidance: Strong candidates name at least 3 models (push for 5+): monthly subscription fee, advertising, premium/freemium account, profile consulting services, micro-transactions (e.g., pay per message, pay to boost profile traffic). Each model should be assessed on pros (revenue certainty, scalability) and cons (adoption rate, user experience impact, dependency on ad revenue cycles, etc.). Candidate should remain structured.

questions.prompt: Grad-U-Date is considering limiting the site to only MBA students. What issues might there be with an MBA-only dating website?
questions.guidance: Key issues: (1) More men than women at most MBA programs — significant gender skew hurts matching quality. (2) Unnecessarily limits market size and app platform scale. (3) Most MBA students tend to be older than other grad students, so many are already married or in a committed relationship, reducing the available dating pool.

questions.prompt: What is the potential market size for Grad-U-Date? [Share Exhibit 1]
questions.guidance: Candidate should use enrollment data from Exhibit 1 and account for program length to estimate total students enrolled at any given time (not just new entrants). Total market = new students per year × years in program, summed across all types, then multiplied by the number of universities.

math.setup: For each program type: total enrolled = new students per year × years in degree. Sum across all programs to get total grad students per university. Multiply by 1,000 universities.

questions.prompt: Calculate the profit of each revenue model. Fixed costs are $10,000,000 per year and variable operating cost is $1 per member per year. Which revenue model would you recommend? [Provide Exhibit 2]
questions.guidance: Candidate must calculate customers, revenue, and profit for all three models and compare. Conclusion from the math: Monthly Fee is most profitable ($25.7M), followed by Premium Account ($20.6M), then Advertising ($16.4M). Candidate should recommend Monthly Fee based solely on this math — but the answer will be revisited with Exhibit 3.

math.setup: Total market = 6,000,000. Fixed cost = $10,000,000/yr. Variable cost = $1 per member per year. Use adoption rates and pricing from Exhibit 2.
steps: 50/50 professional vs non-professional split (from market sizing)
math.answer: Monthly Fee: $25,700,000 profit; Premium Account: $20,600,000 profit; Advertising: $16,400,000 profit

questions.prompt: Does this information change your recommendation for which revenue model? [Provide Exhibit 3]
questions.guidance: Candidate should switch recommendation from monthly fee to premium account. Exhibit 3 shows that the share of users paying a monthly fee and the average monthly fee paid have been declining since 2008 and dropped sharply after 2012. The monthly fee model is therefore at high risk — its current profitability is unlikely to be maintained. The premium account model, while generating less profit today, is more defensible.

questions.prompt: Why do you think that the percentage of users paying monthly fees dropped so quickly starting in 2013?
questions.guidance: Key reasons: (1) Increased competition in the online dating market. (2) Launch of Tinder in late 2012 — a high-quality, convenient, free dating app that disrupted willingness to pay. (3) Proliferation of free dating apps generally from late 2012 onward reduced consumer price expectations.

questions.prompt: Given your recommended revenue model (Premium Account), what other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure ideas into two buckets: reduce costs and increase revenue. Strong answers cover multiple ideas in each bucket.

brainstorming.prompt: What other strategies can Grad-U-Date use to increase profit under the premium account model?

categories.name: Reduce Costs
ideas: Outsource servers to lower infrastructure costs
Provide only email support with no phone support to reduce staffing costs

categories.name: Increase Revenue
ideas: Build a mobile app to attract more customers
Offer profile consulting services for a fee
Partner with popular date-night venues to offer deals (affiliate revenue)
Expand to recent graduate school alumni
Add micro-transactions such as paying to boost profile traffic or send prioritized messages

recommendation: Grad-U-Date should adopt the Premium Account revenue model

The Monthly Fee model generates the highest profit in the current period ($25.7M vs $20.6M for Premium Account), but the monthly fee segment is rapidly shrinking as shown by market trend data — it is unlikely that profitability will be maintained
The Premium Account model is expected to bring in $20,600,000 in annual profit and is more durable given current market dynamics
risks: The premium account share could be seeing a similar decline in adoption as the monthly fee model
A smaller percentage of users may purchase premium accounts than the 40%/20% gender-split forecast
The ad-supported model could be growing faster than the premium account model, making it a better long-term bet
Graduate students may not have sufficient disposable income to pay for premium accounts
The total number of people attending graduate school could decrease, shrinking the addressable market
Graduate students may not want to limit their dating pool to other grad students, reducing adoption
next_steps: Monitor market trends for both the ad-supported and premium account revenue models
Explore expanding into adjacent markets such as undergraduates or international universities
Launch additional revenue services: profile consulting and date-venue partnership deals
Add micro-transactions (e.g., profile traffic boosts) to supplement premium account revenue
Incorporate social media integrations to increase user acquisition and retention
Investigate whether a hybrid premium account + advertising model could work given the single-model constraint
